findings.finding: Two existing host transports have materially different guarantees. ShellEventBus is unbounded and drain collects every queued event into a Vec. NativeEventEmitter already has a bounded single ordered worker and explicit Full/Closed outcomes. Reuse the latter semantics where applicable; do not treat the shell bus as bounded Studio admission.
findings.selected_proposal: Session owns bounded host-neutral job admission; immutable jobs/results carry reservation ownership through completion and snapshot retirement. KernelBindings maps admission/commit/telemetry ports to existing host owners. Separate reserved bounded cancellation/completion capacity from bulk preview work.
findings.rejected_alternative: One global Studio mutex plus unbounded shell notification transport, or assuming queue slot capacity bounds payload bytes.
findings.risk: Slot-bounded queues still permit unbounded payload allocation and waiting-task growth.
findings.mitigation: Admit before allocation/spawn; bound callers, slots and bytes independently; transfer RAII reservations to results and retained generations; return typed overload before accepting an edit.
findings.future_proof: Flood admission with variable payload sizes; demonstrate bounded waiting callers, bytes and result retention; cancel while bulk queue is full; verify completion/stop progress and no silent committed-edit loss.

findings.finding: WP012 already extracted reusable concurrency primitives into handshake_storage_support. Application keyed_lock.rs is a re-export, not a second implementation. guarded_mutation owns a shared wall-clock deadline across keyed lock waits, attempts and sleeps, and observes shutdown cancellation.
findings.selected_proposal: Reuse the published primitive boundary after its canonical standalone lifecycle is resolved; leave actual SurrealDB transactions and error classification with host storage. Session admission must precede document authority acquisition; promotion rechecks principal, grant, revision and idempotency atomically.
findings.rejected_alternative: Copy the keyed-lock/retry implementation into Studio or claim an in-process lock provides distributed/database correctness.
findings.important_distinction: acquire_many_with_deadline retains earlier keyed locks while acquiring later ordered locks and releases them on failure. That algorithm must not be copied as multidimensional byte/resource admission: STU-ARC-012 requires releasing partial resource acquisition before waiting.
findings.risk: Retrying an outcome-unknown commit can duplicate an accepted edit.
findings.mitigation: Bind idempotency to principal/action/canonical payload hash/revision preconditions; reconcile canonical authority after ambiguous acknowledgment. Fence stale worker completions with lease epochs.
findings.future_proof: Independent lock registries over one owning embedded engine; same-key versus disjoint-key overlap; ambiguous commit acknowledgment restart reconciliation; stale epoch rejection; no unrelated write lock for reads.

findings.finding: The general diagnostics recorder takes a buffer mutex and deliberately holds it through the SPSC ring write. Removing this mutex would violate the writer's single-producer discipline. The heartbeat is a separate UI-thread-only lock-free path. Palmistry reads shared memory without writer cooperation.
findings.selected_proposal: Observe emits host-neutral typed counters/outcomes; KernelBindings routes business events to Flight Recorder/EventLedger and allowlisted performance/liveness events to internal_diagnostics. Audio callbacks use preallocated bounded handoff to an off-thread aggregator which invokes the existing recorder.
findings.rejected_alternative: Calling general record() directly from realtime audio, or removing its mutex to advertise lock-free operation.
findings.risk: Existing comments call record non-blocking, but its actual mutex acquisition can wait; it is unsuitable as a realtime guarantee.
findings.mitigation: Keep realtime callback exclusions explicit in human/model manual and public ports; preserve single producer, typed no-content schema and dropped-event accounting.
findings.future_proof: Callback allocation/lock audit, bounded telemetry overflow, audio underrun/discontinuity outcomes, shutdown with active workers, and Palmistry observation while GUI is stalled.

findings.finding: The native MCP already validates a stable client_session_id and derives attributed agent identity from token authority plus that ID. Stable controls/manual/Argus should consume this existing attribution seam instead of introducing another identity registry.
findings.selected_proposal: Controls publishes one capability descriptor consumed by GUI, tools, AccessKit, manuals and Argus; one host adapter reconciles agent_label to client_session_id. Extend existing inspection schema with revision/render/color/proxy/grant provenance rather than adding a parallel Studio debugger.
findings.rejected_alternative: New Studio-only command/manual/inspection registries or per-panel nearly identical controls.
findings.risk: Per-connection 100 requests/sec and 1MiB lines do not by themselves establish aggregate swarm bounds or document/job byte budgets.
findings.mitigation: Add aggregate actor/document/resource admission at existing host seam; preserve independent agent view/selection and operator focus. Existing request identity is attribution, not authorization proof.
findings.future_proof: Multiple attributed clients plus operator; isolated view/focus; stale and revoked grants; control/manual/tool descriptor consistency; fresh screenshot linked to exact action/revision rather than cached visual state.

primary_external_evidence.finding: Bounded MPSC backpressure; clean shutdown closes receiver then consumes remaining messages.
select cancellation of send drops unsent value; reserve permits separate cancellation from payload ownership. Dropping unused permit releases queue capacity.
Owned permits transfer resource lifetime. FIFO acquire_many can head-of-line block smaller requests, so semaphore fairness alone is not actor/document fairness.
Started blocking work cannot be aborted; runtime shutdown timeout does not cancel it. Decoder/render cancellation therefore needs bounded chunks or an explicitly owned provider process boundary.
Child cancellation isolation; cancellation is not atomic while propagation runs. Token cancellation is not a substitute for authoritative lease-epoch fencing.
